title: Why the minstrel show failed; Cootie Williams replaces them
summary: Young's band was too small for a marching minstrel show, with Lee on drums; after they left he hired young Cootie Williams and others.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Just a couple of questions before you get on to talking about the DeParis show.... Anything else you want to say about the vaudeville show? Anything more about the kind of music that was in there and the kind of routines that were done...?
They played the same kind of music on both shows.
But you didn't do any marches in the vaudeville thing.

Oh, no. We just marched on this minstrel show, and we'd make parades. You see, the thing about, why it didn't last long, because Mr. Young didn't have the kind of qualifications for the show. He's supposed to have a big band, like a 12- or 15-piece marching band for that show. He didn't have nothin' but about six or seven pieces.
You mean for the minstrel show.

For the minstrel show. And he had Lee playing drums. Lee was about 10 or 12 years old; he couldn't play no drums -- I mean, for that. And we was marching, you know. He had two trombones and three trumpets and a clarinet. See, that was a marching band. He didn't have a bass horn... No, we didn't even have no bass horn, because my brother had left.
When did your brother leave?
My brother left at Pensacola, Florida.
Clarence left the minstrel show in Pensacola, Florida.
No, he left the vaudeville show in
Phillips - 42

Pensacola, Florida. We had about seven or eight pieces marching, but that ain't no marching band. Then he didn't have... He was putting out the kind of money that's supposed to have in minstrel shows... You're supposed to have about maybe 50 or 60 people in a minstrel show. He didn't have no more than about 15. So it didn't go over. So it folded up in Mobile, Alabama, and then we left and he got Cootie and them in our place.
Who?
Cootie. Cootie Williams.
Mr. Young got Cootie Williams to fill in?
He got Cootie... They was young. Cootie was about 16. He got Cootie and he got Cootie's brother, who was playing trombone.
What was his name?
I don't know his name. See, these guys was in the band... They came after we left. Cootie, and he had another guy named Ralph (I forget his last name) -- he was playing trumpet.
And all the Youngs, of course, were still in the band. None of them left.
Oh no! They was too young.
And. Mrs. Young was still with them, right?
